atAGlance: Bún mắm is a Mekong-style noodle soup with fermented fish broth, rice vermicelli, seafood, pork, eggplant, herbs, and a deep salty aroma. It is bold on purpose.
whatItIs: Bún mắm is rice vermicelli in fermented fish broth with seafood, pork, eggplant, herbs, and a powerful savory aroma. It is one of the boldest soups in the menu set.
howToEnjoy: Smell and sip before adding chili. Herbs and vegetables are not decoration; they freshen the fermented fish broth.
howLocalsOrder: Bún mắm is for people who want the fermented fish broth, so ask what seafood is in today's pot before committing. Less chili and no pork are worth saying early because toppings are added fast.
worthKnowing: Bún mắm is strongly associated with southern and Mekong Delta cooking. The fermented fish base is the identity, not a flaw.
goodToKnow: This is one of the strongest-flavored soups on a Vietnamese menu. If fermented fish sounds like too much, choose bún riêu or phở first.
regionalAssociation: southern Vietnam and the Mekong Delta
travelerCaution: Contains fermented fish broth and often seafood or pork.
